title: Twenty First Word First Station First Warning Imagined Permanence And Lifes Shortness

questions.question: What mistaken idea is the nafs blamed for in the First Warning?
questions.answer: It acts as if life in this world will last a long time or never end.

questions.question: What two short time periods are mentioned to show how uncertain life is?
questions.answer: Even reaching the next year or the next day is not guaranteed.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the real reason the nafs gets bored with worship?
questions.answer: It wrongly assumes there will always be more time later.

questions.question: How is human life described in relation to time?
questions.answer: It is short and quickly passing away.

questions.question: How much of the day is described as being spent in worship?
questions.answer: One hour out of twenty-four.

questions.question: How is that hour of worship characterized?
questions.answer: It is presented as good, manageable, gentle, and beneficial.

questions.question: What lasting benefit is connected to that act of worship?
questions.answer: It helps a person gain the true happiness of the life to come.

questions.question: If a person truly understood the shortness of life, how would that affect his attitude toward prayer?
questions.answer: He would feel eager and pleased instead of tired of it.

questions.question: Who is being addressed in the First Warning?
questions.answer: The person’s own nafs, meaning the lower self.

questions.question: Why does the speaker question whether the nafs has proof of living longer?
questions.answer: To show that it has no certainty about the future.

questions.question: What attitude toward worldly enjoyment is criticized?
questions.answer: Wanting to keep enjoying this world as if it will continue forever.

questions.question: What false assumption turns worship into something annoying for the nafs?
questions.answer: The assumption that there will always be plenty of time later.

questions.question: What is the one-hour act meant to achieve beyond this worldly life?
questions.answer: It is a means to eternal success and real happiness.

questions.question: What emotional change is expected when a person understands the truth correctly?
questions.answer: Boredom should change into sincere desire and joy.

questions.question: What is the first challenge made to the nafs in this warning?
questions.answer: It is challenged to prove that its life will continue.

questions.question: Why is asking for proof about tomorrow important in the argument?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that even the near future is not in human control.

questions.question: What kind of outlook makes the nafs complain?
questions.answer: A careless outlook that treats temporary life as if it were permanent.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is happening to life even while a person delays worship?
questions.answer: It is passing away and being lost.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of a single hour?
questions.answer: A small amount of time can have great spiritual value if used properly.

questions.question: Which is presented as more reasonable: chasing endless comfort in this world or worshipping for eternal benefit?
questions.answer: Worshipping for eternal benefit is presented as more reasonable.

questions.question: What words best describe the act of worship in this passage: harsh and heavy, or pleasant and merciful?
questions.answer: Pleasant and merciful.

questions.question: What does the phrase about true happiness point toward?
questions.answer: It points toward success in the eternal life, not just temporary worldly comfort.

questions.question: What inference can be made about procrastination from this warning?
questions.answer: Delaying worship is foolish because no one is promised more time.

questions.question: How does this warning try to reform the nafs?
questions.answer: It corrects its false hope of long life and teaches it to value immediate obedience.

questions.question: What is the main problem in the nafs’s thinking according to the First Warning?
questions.answer: It misunderstands the nature of life by treating it as if it were endless.

questions.question: How does the passage weaken the excuse of boredom?
questions.answer: It shows that boredom comes from illusion, not from worship itself.

questions.question: What role does uncertainty about death play in the warning?
questions.answer: It pushes the reader to act now instead of assuming there will be later opportunities.

questions.question: What is being contrasted when the passage mentions one hour and twenty-four hours?
questions.answer: A very small daily effort is being compared with the whole day to show how reasonable worship is.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about wasting time?
questions.answer: It means letting a short life pass without gaining real benefit from it.

questions.question: Why is worship described in positive terms rather than as a burden?
questions.answer: To show that it is a mercy and a source of good, not something crushing.

questions.question: What is the relationship between worship and eternal life in this passage?
questions.answer: Worship is presented as a path leading to lasting happiness in the next life.

questions.question: How should a wise person respond to the shortness of life?
questions.answer: By using time carefully and giving proper attention to worship.

questions.question: What inner change is expected if the nafs understands this message?
questions.answer: Complaining should turn into willing and joyful devotion.

questions.question: What question is used to shake the nafs out of heedlessness?
questions.answer: Whether it really thinks its life will continue for a long time.

questions.question: What illusion causes the nafs to resent acts of worship?
questions.answer: The illusion that worldly life is long enough to delay serious obedience.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the direction of life’s movement?
questions.answer: It is moving away and not staying.

questions.question: How much time is asked for in worship compared with the rest of the day?
questions.answer: Only a small portion of the day is asked for.

questions.question: What future result gives that small daily act such great importance?
questions.answer: It can lead to the real joy of eternal life.

questions.question: What criticism of worldly-mindedness is implied here?
questions.answer: It focuses too much on temporary comfort and too little on the hereafter.

questions.question: What practical lesson can a Muslim student apply from this warning?
questions.answer: Do not delay prayer or treat it like a burden, because life is uncertain and worship brings lasting benefit.

questions.question: In the First Warning, what is the nafs unable to guarantee?
questions.answer: Its continued life even into the near future.

questions.question: What mental habit leads the nafs to become tired of worship?
questions.answer: Imagining a long, ongoing worldly life.

questions.question: What does the warning reveal about the connection between wrong beliefs and wrong feelings?
questions.answer: False beliefs about life produce negative feelings like boredom toward worship.

questions.question: What is the condition of life as described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is brief and steadily slipping away.

questions.question: Why is dedicating one hour of the day to worship presented as fair?
questions.answer: Because it is a small amount of time for something with immense benefit.

questions.question: What reward is greater than temporary enjoyment in this world?
questions.answer: The real happiness of everlasting life.

questions.question: How does the passage appeal both to reason and to emotion?
questions.answer: It uses logic about life’s uncertainty and also encourages a heartfelt desire for eternal happiness.

questions.question: What should replace boredom once the truth is understood?
questions.answer: Cheerful readiness and sincere enthusiasm.

questions.question: What is the central message of this warning for a believer?
questions.answer: Since life is short and uncertain, regular worship is not too much to ask but a wise use of time that leads to eternal good.
